records.source: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ εἶδον ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου·
records.gloss: And the fifth angel blew trumpet, and I saw a star out of the heaven having fallen to the earth, and was given to him the key of the shaft of the abyss.
pieces: When the fifth angel blew his trumpet, I saw a star that had fallen from the sky to the earth, and to him was given the key to the shaft that leads down into the abyss.

L.1: And the fifth angel blew his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and the key of the shaft of the abyss was given to him.

R.1: The fifth angel blew his trumpet. I saw a star that had fallen from the sky to the earth. The star was given the key to the opening of the bottomless pit.

decisions.choice: a fallen star: an angelic being
alternatives: a fallen, evil angel, like the star of Isaiah 14:12
an angel sent by God, like the one with the key in 20:1
decisions.reason: The star is a person: it is given a key and opens the pit. Stars stand for angels in 1:20. πεπτωκότα, "having fallen", may mean a fallen angel (Isaiah 14:12; Luke 10:18), or simply one that has come down; in 20:1 an angel who comes down from heaven holds the key to the abyss and binds Satan. Either way, the key is given: the pit is opened only by God's leave.

decisions.choice: the abyss: the deep prison of evil powers
decisions.reason: ἀβύσσου means the bottomless deep. In the New Testament it is the place where demons are confined (Luke 8:31), the beast comes up from it (11:7; 17:8), and Satan is locked in it (20:1-3). A φρέατος is a shaft or well leading down into it.

decisions.choice: abyss (L, B); bottomless pit (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Greek word, which English has borrowed; Readable says what it is.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: As in chapter 8, every level says that the angel blew his trumpet.

records.heading: The fifth trumpet: locusts from the abyss

records.source: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου μεγάλης, καὶ ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος.
records.gloss: And he opened the shaft of the abyss, and went up smoke out of the shaft like smoke of furnace great, and was darkened the sun and the air by the smoke of the shaft.
pieces: He opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke rose from it like smoke from a huge furnace; the sun and the air grew dark with the smoke from the shaft.

L.2: And he opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke went up from the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the shaft.

R.2: He opened it, and smoke poured out like smoke from a huge furnace. The smoke made the sun and the sky dark.

decisions.choice: smoke like a furnace: Sodom and Sinai
decisions.reason: When God destroyed Sodom, the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a furnace (Genesis 19:28), and Sinai smoked like a furnace when God came down on it (Exodus 19:18).

records.source: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐταῖς ἐξουσία ὡς ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And out of the smoke came out locusts into the earth, and was given to them authority as have authority the scorpions of the earth.
pieces: From the smoke locusts swarmed out over the earth, and they were given the kind of power scorpions have.

L.3: And out of the smoke locusts came out onto the earth, and power was given to them like the power that the scorpions of the earth have.

R.3: Locusts came out of the smoke and spread over the earth. They were given power to sting like scorpions.

decisions.choice: locusts: the eighth plague of Egypt and Joel's army
decisions.reason: A swarm of locusts was one of the plagues of Egypt (Exodus 10:12-15), and Joel describes a locust plague as an invading army on the day of the LORD (Joel 1-2). These locusts come from the abyss and are not ordinary insects.

decisions.choice: scorpions: a painful sting, rarely deadly
decisions.reason: The sting of a scorpion causes great pain but seldom kills an adult, which fits 9:5-6.

records.source: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐταῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον, εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων.
records.gloss: And it was said to them that not they will harm the grass of the earth nor any green thing nor any tree, except the men who not have the seal of the God on the foreheads.
pieces: Their orders were to leave alone the earth's grass, every green plant, and every tree, and to harm only the {{gender:people|men}} without the seal of God on their foreheads.

L.4: And they were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any green thing or any tree, but only the {{gender:people|men}} who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.

R.4: They were told not to hurt the grass or plants or trees. They could only hurt the {{gender:people|men}} who did not have God's mark on their foreheads.

decisions.choice: not the plants: locusts unlike any natural swarm
decisions.reason: Natural locusts eat every green thing. These are told to leave plants alone and to harm only people, which shows that they are not ordinary locusts.

decisions.choice: those with God's seal are protected
decisions.reason: The seal of 7:2-3 protects God's slaves from this plague, as the Israelites in Goshen were spared the plagues of Egypt (Exodus 8:22; 10:23). The protection is from God's judgments; elsewhere believers still suffer at the hands of the world (6:9-11; 13:7).

decisions.choice: people | men; humankind | mankind
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, so it takes the gender setting.

records.source: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς, ἀλλ’ ἵνα βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε· καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου, ὅταν παίσῃ ἄνθρωπον.
records.gloss: And it was given to them that not they kill them, but that they will be tormented months five; and the torment of them as torment of scorpion when it strikes a man.
pieces: Killing them was not permitted; the locusts could only torment them for five months, and the pain they caused was like the pain of a scorpion's sting on {{gender:a person|a man}}.

L.5: And it was given to them not to kill them, but that they would be tormented five months, and their torment [was] like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes {{gender:a person|a man}}.

R.5: The locusts were not allowed to kill those people. They could only make them suffer for five months. The pain was like the pain of a scorpion's sting.

decisions.choice: five months: a limited time
alternatives: the life of a locust, from spring to late summer
decisions.reason: Five months may be the season of locusts, or simply a set and limited time. The suffering is real, and it has an end.

decisions.choice: allowed: limited by God
decisions.reason: As with the riders of chapter 6, "it was given" shows that the locusts act only within the limits God sets: they may torment but not kill.

records.source: καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνατον καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρήσουσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐπιθυμήσουσιν ἀποθανεῖν καὶ φεύγει ὁ θάνατος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And in the days those will seek the men the death and not not will find it, and they will long to die, and flees the death from them.
pieces: During those days {{gender:people|men}} will search for death, but it will not be found; they will want to die, and death will keep fleeing from them.

L.6: And in those days {{gender:people|men}} will seek death and will certainly not find it, and they will long to die, and death flees from them.

R.6: During that time {{gender:people|men}} will want to die, but they will not be able to. They will wish they were dead, but death will run away from them.

decisions.choice: longing for death: Job and Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Job speaks of those who long for death and it does not come, who dig for it more than for hidden treasure (Job 3:21). Jeremiah says that death will be preferred to life (Jeremiah 8:3).

decisions.choice: people | men; humankind | mankind
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, so it takes the gender setting.

records.source: Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι ὅμοιοι χρυσῷ, καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων, καὶ εἶχον τρίχας ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν, καὶ εἶχον θώρακας ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον·
records.gloss: And the likenesses of the locusts like to horses having been prepared for battle, and on the heads of them as crowns like to gold, and the faces of them as faces of men, \v 8 and they had hair as hair of women, and the teeth of them as of lions were, \v 9 and they had breastplates as breastplates iron, and the sound of the wings of them as sound of chariots of horses many running into battle.
pieces: In shape the locusts were like horses made ready for war. They had what looked like gold crowns on their heads, and their faces were like the faces of human beings.
Their hair was like a woman's hair, their teeth like a lion's.
Their chests were armored as if with iron breastplates, and their wings made a noise like chariots and many horses charging into battle.

L.7: And the appearance of the locusts [was] like horses prepared for battle, and on their heads [was something] like crowns like gold, and their faces [were] like human faces,
L.8: and they had hair like women's hair, and their teeth were like lions' [teeth],
L.9: and they had breastplates like iron breastplates, and the sound of their wings [was] like the sound of chariots of many horses running into battle.

R.7: The locusts looked like horses ready for war. On their heads they had something like gold crowns. Their faces looked like people's faces.
R.8: They had long hair like women. They had teeth like lions.
R.9: Their chests were covered with something like iron armor. The noise their wings made was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.

decisions.choice: Joel's locust army
decisions.reason: Joel 2:4-5 says the locusts look like horses and run like war horses, with a noise like chariots, and Joel 1:6 says they have the teeth of a lion. John builds on Joel's picture.

decisions.choice: "like", again and again: a vision described by comparisons
decisions.reason: Nearly every feature is introduced with "like". John describes what he saw as best he can, and the creatures are a mixture of the human, the animal and the military: a demonic army, not a natural swarm.

decisions.choice: the description divided into sentences (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:14-16, Balanced and Readable supply the verbs the Greek leaves out and divide the long list.

records.source: καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα, καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε.
records.gloss: And they have tails like to scorpions and stings, and in the tails of them the authority of them to harm the men months five.
pieces: Like scorpions they have tails with stings, and it is with their tails that they have power to harm {{gender:people|men}} for five months.

L.10: And they have tails like scorpions, and stings, and in their tails [is] their power to harm {{gender:people|men}} for five months.

R.10: They had tails with stingers like scorpions. Their tails gave them power to hurt {{gender:people|men}} for five months.

decisions.choice: they have: John switches to the present
decisions.reason: ἔχουσιν is present, as if the vision were before his eyes again.

decisions.choice: people | men; humankind | mankind
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, so it takes the gender setting.

records.source: ἔχουσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν βασιλέα τὸν ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου· ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει Ἀπολλύων.
records.gloss: They have over them king the angel of the abyss; name to him in Hebrew Abaddon, and in the Greek name he has Apollyon.
pieces: Over them they have a king, the angel of the abyss. In Hebrew his name is Abaddon, and in Greek he is called Apollyon.

L.11: They have over them [as] king the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew [is] Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.

R.11: Their king is the angel in charge of the bottomless pit. His name in Hebrew is Abaddon. In Greek his name is Apollyon. Both names mean Destroyer.

decisions.choice: Abaddon and Apollyon: Destruction and Destroyer
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew Bible Abaddon means destruction and is a name for the realm of the dead (Job 26:6; 28:22; Psalm 88:12). Apollyon is a Greek word meaning "destroyer". The king of the locusts is named for what he does.

decisions.choice: Apollyon and Apollo
decisions.reason: The name sounds like Apollo, a god whose symbols included the locust, and some emperors associated themselves with Apollo. John may intend the echo, but he does not say so.

decisions.choice: locusts with a king
decisions.reason: Proverbs 30:27 says that locusts have no king, yet they advance in ranks. These locusts have one, which marks them again as more than locusts.

decisions.choice: Both names mean Destroyer (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the names mean (m1).

records.source: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ μία ἀπῆλθεν· ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο οὐαὶ μετὰ ταῦτα.
records.gloss: The woe the first has passed; behold come yet two woes after these things.
pieces: The first woe is over. Look: two woes are still to come after this.

L.12: The first woe has passed; look, two woes are still coming after these things.

R.12: The first terrible thing is over. But two more terrible things are still coming.

decisions.choice: the first woe is the fifth trumpet
decisions.reason: The eagle announced three woes for the last three trumpets (8:13). The locusts are the first; the second follows with the sixth trumpet (11:14).

decisions.choice: "after these things" ends 9:12
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT takes "after these things" with the woes still to come. Some editions begin 9:13 with it. The sense hardly changes.

decisions.choice: woe (L, B); terrible thing (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:13.

records.source: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, λέγοντα τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀγγέλῳ, ὁ ἔχων τὴν σάλπιγγα· Λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ.
records.gloss: And the sixth angel blew trumpet, and I heard voice one out of the horns of the altar the golden the [one] before the God, \v 14 saying to the sixth angel, the [one] having the trumpet: Release the four angels the [ones] having been bound at the river the great Euphrates.
pieces: Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard a single voice from the horns of the gold altar that stands before God.
It said to the sixth angel, who held the trumpet, "Set free the four angels who are held bound beside the great river, the Euphrates."

L.13: And the sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar that is before God,
L.14: saying to the sixth angel, the one who had the trumpet, "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates."

R.13: The sixth angel blew his trumpet. Then I heard a voice coming from the corners of the gold altar in front of God.
R.14: It spoke to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet. It said, "Let the four angels go free. They have been tied up at the great Euphrates River."

decisions.choice: from the horns of the altar
alternatives: from the four horns of the altar
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "from the horns". Many manuscripts read "from the four horns". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a voice from the altar: the prayers answered
decisions.reason: The golden altar is where the prayers of the saints rose (8:3-5). The command comes from there: the judgments answer the prayers of God's people. The altar's horns were its raised corners (Exodus 30:2-3).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates: the frontier from which invaders came
decisions.reason: The Euphrates was the eastern limit of the land promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18) and, in John's day, the border between the Roman Empire and the Parthians. Assyria and Babylon had come against Israel from beyond it (Isaiah 8:7).

decisions.choice: horns (L, B); corners (R)
decisions.reason: The horns of an altar were its four raised corners; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: As in chapter 8, every level says that the angel blew his trumpet.

records.heading: The sixth trumpet: the army from the Euphrates

records.source: καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: And were released the four angels the [ones] having been prepared for the hour and day and month and year, so that they might kill the third of the men.
pieces: The four angels were set loose. They had been made ready for that hour, that day, month, and year, to kill a third of {{gender:humankind|mankind}}.

L.15: And the four angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour and day and month and year, to kill a third of {{gender:humankind|mankind}}.

R.15: So the four angels were set free. God had kept them ready for this exact hour, day, month, and year. They were set free to kill a third of all {{gender:people|men}}.

decisions.choice: prepared for the hour: God's appointed time
decisions.reason: The single article over "hour and day and month and year" points to one exact moment, fixed in advance. Even the release of destruction happens only at the time God has set.

decisions.choice: God had kept them ready (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who prepared them, which the passive implies (m1).

decisions.choice: people | men; humankind | mankind
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, so it takes the gender setting.

records.source: καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ἱππικοῦ δισμυριάδες μυριάδων· ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And the number of the armies of the cavalry two myriads of myriads; I heard the number of them.
pieces: Their mounted armies numbered 200,000,000; I heard the count.

L.16: And the number of the armies of the cavalry [was] two myriads of myriads; I heard their number.

R.16: I heard how many soldiers on horses there were. There were 200,000,000 of them.

decisions.choice: two myriads of myriads: an immense army
decisions.reason: A myriad is ten thousand, so the number is two hundred million. It is far beyond any army of the ancient world, and it means a force too great to imagine (compare Psalm 68:18; Daniel 7:10).

decisions.choice: two myriads of myriads (L); 200,000,000 (B, R)
alternatives: twice ten thousand times ten thousand
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek words; Balanced and Readable give the number in figures, as the style guide does for large numbers.

records.source: καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπ’ αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις· καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων, καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον.
records.gloss: And thus I saw the horses in the vision and those sitting on them, having breastplates fiery and hyacinth and sulfurous; and the heads of the horses as heads of lions, and out of the mouths of them comes out fire and smoke and sulfur.
pieces: This is how I saw the horses and their riders in my vision. The riders wore breastplates the colors of fire, of dark blue hyacinth, and of yellow sulfur. The horses' heads were like lions' heads, and fire, smoke, and sulfur poured from their mouths.

L.17: And thus I saw the horses in the vision and those seated on them, having breastplates fiery red and hyacinth blue and sulfur yellow, and the heads of the horses [were] like heads of lions, and out of their mouths come fire and smoke and sulfur.

R.17: In my vision I saw the horses and their riders. The riders wore armor that was red like fire, dark blue, and yellow like sulfur. The horses had heads like lions. Fire, smoke, and burning sulfur came out of their mouths.

decisions.choice: three colors that match the fire, smoke and sulfur
decisions.reason: πυρίνους is fiery red, ὑακινθίνους the dark blue of the hyacinth stone or smoke, and θειώδεις sulfur yellow. They match the fire, smoke and sulfur that come from the horses' mouths.

decisions.choice: fire and sulfur: the judgment of Sodom
decisions.reason: God rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24). In Revelation fire and sulfur belong to the final judgment (14:10; 19:20; 21:8).

decisions.choice: whose breastplates: most likely the riders'
decisions.reason: ἔχοντας agrees with "those seated on them", so it is most likely the riders who wear the breastplates.

decisions.choice: sulfur
decisions.reason: "Brimstone" is the older English word for sulfur.

records.source: ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: By the three plagues these was killed the third of the men, by the fire and the smoke and the sulfur the [one] coming out out of the mouths of them.
pieces: These three plagues, the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur coming out of their mouths, killed a third of {{gender:humankind|mankind}}.

L.18: By these three plagues a third of {{gender:humankind|mankind}} was killed, by the fire and the smoke and the sulfur that came out of their mouths.

R.18: These three terrible things killed a third of all {{gender:people|men}}: the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur that came out of the horses' mouths.

decisions.choice: three plagues: fire, smoke and sulfur
decisions.reason: πληγῶν means a blow or plague, the word used of the plagues of Egypt in the Greek Old Testament. Here it names the fire, smoke and sulfur of 9:17.

decisions.choice: people | men; humankind | mankind
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, so it takes the gender setting.

records.source: ἡ γὰρ ἐξουσία τῶν ἵππων ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν· αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ὄφεσιν, ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς, καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν.
records.gloss: For the authority of the horses in the mouth of them is and in the tails of them; for the tails of them like to serpents, having heads, and with them they harm.
pieces: It is in their mouths that the horses' power lies, and in their tails too, for their tails are like snakes with heads, and with these they wound.

L.19: For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails, for their tails [are] like serpents, having heads, and with them they do harm.

R.19: The horses could hurt people with their mouths and with their tails. Their tails were like snakes, with heads that bit people.

decisions.choice: tails like serpents: a further picture of harm
decisions.reason: The locusts stung with their tails (9:10); these horses bite with tails like snakes. The serpent recalls the ancient enemy (12:9).

records.source: Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἳ οὐκ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν ταῖς πληγαῖς ταύταις, οὐδὲ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ προσκυνήσουσιν τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ χρυσᾶ καὶ τὰ ἀργυρᾶ καὶ τὰ χαλκᾶ καὶ τὰ λίθινα καὶ τὰ ξύλινα, ἃ οὔτε βλέπειν δύνανται οὔτε ἀκούειν οὔτε περιπατεῖν, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν φόνων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν φαρμάκων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And the rest of the men, who not were killed by the plagues these, not even repented of the works of the hands of them, that not they will worship the demons and the idols the golden and the silver and the bronze and the stone and the wooden, which neither to see are able nor to hear nor to walk, \v 21 and not they repented of the murders of them nor of the sorceries of them nor of the sexual immorality of them nor of the thefts of them.
pieces: Yet the rest of {{gender:humankind|mankind}}, who survived these plagues, did not repent and turn from the things their own hands had made: they went on worshiping demons, and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood that have no power to see or hear or walk.
There was no repentance for their murders or their sorcery, for their sexual immorality or their stealing.

L.20: And the rest of {{gender:humankind|mankind}}, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, so as not to worship demons and idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk,
L.21: and they did not repent of their murders or of their sorceries or of their sexual immorality or of their thefts.

R.20: But the {{gender:people|men}} who were not killed by these plagues still did not change. They kept worshiping demons. They kept worshiping idols made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, idols that cannot see or hear or walk.
R.21: They did not stop murdering people, using magic, committing sexual sins, or stealing.

decisions.choice: the plagues call for repentance, and are refused
decisions.reason: The trumpets are warnings: they strike only a part of the world, and their purpose is repentance. But those who survive harden themselves, as Pharaoh did after each plague (Exodus 8:15, 32). In 11:13 some do give glory to God.

decisions.choice: idols that cannot see, hear or walk: Psalm 115 and Daniel 5
decisions.reason: Psalm 115:4-7 mocks idols of silver and gold that have eyes but cannot see, ears but cannot hear, feet but cannot walk. Daniel 5:23 lists gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone. Behind the idols stand demons (Deuteronomy 32:17; 1 Corinthians 10:20).

decisions.choice: sorceries: magic, often with potions
decisions.reason: φαρμάκων comes from a word for drugs or potions, and it means magic and sorcery. It is linked with idolatry in 18:23 and 22:15.

decisions.choice: sorceries (L); sorcery (B); using magic (R)
decisions.reason: The levels name the practice in plain words (m3).

decisions.choice: people | men; humankind | mankind
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, so it takes the gender setting.
